newsitem.title: THAILAND: Protesters block exits from Thai PM's office.
newsitem.headline: Protesters block exits from Thai PM's office.

text.p: Thousands of noisy and frustrated Thai protesters on Tuesday ringed Government House where the prime minister's office is located and blocked most exits from the building, police said.
An estimated 15,000 villagers have been camping around the building since they streamed into the capital in late January from the impoverished northeast Thailand to demand social justice.

"The mob has blocked most exits from Government House and refused to leave until Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh comes out to meet them to discuss their demands," a government official told Reuters.
The premier was still in his office but it was unclear if he was going to meet them. There were also several other cabinet ministers in the building.
Chavalit told reporters from inside Government House that he recognised the villagers had problems that needed to be solved.
"We have to heed their demands and appreciate their hardships but sometimes things cannot be done quickly and they should understand this," he said.
He declined to say what action he planned to take.
About 300 anti-riot police were put on alert at the scene, although they did not spring into action, eyewitnesses said.
Spokesmen for the protesters told Reuters they were dissatisfied with a lack of progress in their negotiations with the government on settling their demands.
They wanted to see the premier to seek some sort of a settlement.
The protesters, organised by a movement called the Assembly of the Poor, want to be released from indebtedness to the state-owned Agriculture and Cooperatives Bank.
They are also seeking higher prices for their farm produce and settlement of their land disputes with the government.
The group has been living in makeshift tents, cooking their food and bathing on the street in the scorching April heat.
